General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Elle ↗ Open Full Page

Ariana Grande’s Eternal Sunshine Tour Is Getting a Concert Film and Documentary

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ariana Grande’s Eternal Sunshine Tour may have wrapped in September, but fans will soon get another chance to experience it.
  • The news comes nearly three months after Grande concluded her first concert tour in seven years, an experience she has previously described as a significant chapter in her career.
  • Here’s everything we know about the projects so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ariana Grande’s Eternal Sunshine Tour may have wrapped in September, but fans will soon get another chance to experience it. Following an initial teaser on November 23, the singer announced on November 24 that both a concert film and a documentary for the tour are set to premiere on Peacock.

The news comes nearly three months after Grande concluded her first concert tour in seven years, an experience she has previously described as a significant chapter in her career.

Here’s everything we know about the projects so far.

According to recent reports, the documentary—titled The Eternal Sunshine Diaries: The Making of the Tour —follows Grande “during the 30 days leading up to the opening of her sold-out tour as she and her team race to bring the ambitious production to life,” according to Peacock. “At the same time, Grande is putting the finishing touches on her eighth studio album, giving audiences an intimate window into her creative process during a pivotal moment.”.

The Eternal Sunshine Tour concert film “journeys through the collapse of her reality, a cosmic rebirth, a reconnection with her inner child, and the memories that shaped her. She transforms the Eternal Sunshine Tour into a cinematic celebration of healing, connection, and the music that has defined her life.”.

Her Eternal Sunshine Tour began in Oakland, California, on June 6 and concluded on September 1 following 10 performances at London’s O2 Arena. The reveals featured music from across her discography, including Eternal Sunshine, Positions, and her latest album, Petal, which was released in July.

The tour also marked Grande’s return to the concert stage following her 2019 Sweetener World Tour. Throughout the run, she performed in custom looks from designers including Alexander McQueen, Givenchy, and Vivienne Westwood, styled by Law Roach.

Grande shared the first teaser on Instagram on November 23, in collaboration with Peacock and Team Ariana.

The video features footage of Grande performing the title track from Eternal Sunshine. As the performance ends, the screen reveals the message: “Coming soon to… Peacock.”.

During an August interview with Vosk in the City, Grande reflected on how her latest tour differed from her previous experiences performing live.

“I think my last tour I wasn’t necessarily in the same place in life, and I wasn’t able to be as present as I am this time,” she explained, describing the Eternal Sunshine Tour as “such a beautiful corrective experience.”.

Grande also spoke about reconnecting with longtime fans through songs spanning more than a decade of her career.

Industry observers note that in August, her representative confirmed that the singer planned to step away from public-facing work following the tour. Grande later addressed the decision during a concert in Chicago, explaining that it had been made well in advance.

“It is something that I have decided; it’s a plan that I had quietly made a long time ago, and it’s a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place,” she told the audience.

The Eternal Sunshine Diaries: The Making of the Tour documentary premieres on Peacock on December 11. The Eternal Sunshine Tour concert film arrives on December 12.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the ’80s film Blade Runner is the latest to get the streaming series treatment, after the legacy sequel Blade Runner 2049 revitalized the science fiction noir franchise about humanoid robots called “replicants” that slowly took over society back in 2017. The fresh series takes place 80 years after that original film. What’s changed? Who’s in charge now? Before you press play on Blade Runner 2099, let’s run through the cast and characters.

This is the official description of the series from Prime Video:.

Which of the new characters are human? Which ones are replicants? Does it even matter anymore? Here’s what you need to know.

Olwen is an old-school replicant Blade Runner on the verge of retirement.

Michelle Yeoh is a former pageant queen, ballet dancer, and Academy Award-winning actress. You know her from Everything Everywhere All At Once, Wicked, Crazy Rich Asians, Memoirs of a Geisha, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, Star Trek: Discovery, American Born Chinese, and Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon. She is also a Golden Globe, Critics Choice, and Actor Award winner. Before all of that, she had a prolific Hong Kong action and martial arts filmography. Legend!

Cora is a replicant who goes undercover as a human.

Hunter Schafer is a model and actress best known for playing Jules on Euphoria. She played President Snow’s cousin Tigris in The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes and followed that up with the films Cuckoo, Kinds of Kindness, and Mother Mary. Next, you’ll see her in the upcoming Tom Ford movie Cry to Heaven, adapted from Anne Rice’s historical novel.

Bebeto is a human who teams up with Cora.

Dimitri played Reaper, a District 11 tribute, in The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. Some of his other credits include four episodes of the Netflix series Warrior Nun, the Prime Video series Love Addicts, the Apple TV+ series Hijack, and a decent smattering of productions in his home country, Germany.

Elias is Cora’s younger brother.

Recent findings suggest that lewis starred as Danny in the drama series Somewhere Boy. You might also recognize him from Masters of the Air, Generation Z, Shetland, and Silent Witness. He played a young version of Peter Capaldi’s character in the Black Mirror episode “Plaything.” His film credits include gnarly horror movies like The Severed Sun and The Damned. Next you’ll see him in the ensemble cast of Lorna Tucker’s Bare.

Yahya is another replicant Blade Runner.

Matthew is best known for playing Larys Strong on House of the Dragon. (His co-star Freddie Fox also appears in the Blade Runner 2099 pilot.) He also played Lucien Bonaparte in Ridley Scott’s film Napoleon, and starred in the medical drama series Casualty. If you’re a historical drama junkie, you might know him as Mr. Crowe from Sanditon and/or Mr. Drummie from the 2023 Great Expectations.

Helena is a very mysterious character you’ll glimpse in the first episode.

Sources indicate that sheila Atim is an Olivier Award-winning actress for her supporting role in the Bob Dylan jukebox musical Girl from the North Country. You might recognize her from films and shows like Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, The Woman King, Harlots, and The Underground Railroad. Atim debuted as Akasha in The Vampire Lestat, aka Interview with the Vampire season 3, and will take center stage when the AMC series rebrands to adapt Anne Rice’s Queen of the Damned in season 4.

Tom Burke is a stage and screen actor who played Praetorian Jack in Furiosa and Orson Welles in Mank. His other film credits include The Souvenir, The Souvenir Part II, Living, The Wonder, and Black Bag. Some of his television credits include Jerico, The Hour, and classic literary adaptations like War & Peace, Great Expectations, and The Musketeers. You’ll see him next in Robert Eggers’ Werwulf and the upcoming Elden Ring movie.

This character is a bit of a mystery!

Daniel is a BAFTA-winning actor for the television film Eric and Ernie. You might recognize him from Flowers, Jericho, Watership Down, Sick Note, and Renegade Nell. He also does a lot of stage acting, including a one-man show, and previously worked as a stand-up comedian.

Amy Lennox is a prolific West End theater actress who was nominated for an Olivier Award in 2016. She played Chloe Godard on 100 episodes of the medical drama Holby City and also starred in the short-lived sitcom Only Child.

Katelyn Rose Downey plays Greta.

You’ll meet this mysterious character in the first episode.

Katelyn is an Irish actress you may have seen before in The Princess with Joey King, the murder mystery series Clean Sweep, or The Nun II.

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

It has been revealed that welcome to the Esquire Endorsement. Heavily researched. Thoroughly vetted. These picks are the best way to spend your hard-earned cash.

Industry observers note that in my life, I lean toward luxury and secondhand clothing wherever possible, desperately trying to get away from all the cheap garbage being sold to me on Instagram ads and the Amazon homepage. I’ve spent years of my life hunting sales and eBay listings for clothes and boots. I’m like an edge-habitat pine growing in the direction of the radiant sun that is well-made clothing, trying to forget the fast fashion slop that lies in the forest behind me.

In a recent development, but I throw that out the window when it comes to sneakers. Designer sneakers are, for me, one of the dumbest things I could ever buy. Even when they are made with real leather, you are paying for a plastic sole that has a lifespan of a few years. I don’t think you should pay more than the $200 price of a pair of Latest Balance when it comes to sneakers.

Under that price point, I’ve never been able to find a good pair German Army Trainers, which I have always wanted. That changed when I found these. Quince (yeah yeah, I was just complaining about fashion slop, but life is full of contradictions) makes a perfect pair of GATs—and it makes them for $95. I honestly think every man in the world should buy a pair of these.

This is my real qualm with designer sneakers, and it totally undercuts anything you could tell me about the second-hand sneaker hype market. What you should pay for, when you pay expensive prices for clothing, is craftsmanship. When you buy a Gucci 1953 loafer or Loro Piana cashmere you probably arrived there because of the brand, but you are paying for the craftsmanship. I see no such correlation in designer sneakers, even the ones those brands make.

According to recent reports, but a $95 pair of kicks? That’s honest. Even though I’m not bullish on Quince’s fast fashion take on quiet luxury (nor am I bullish on its caviar program), and the fact that Quince chose to closely replicate the Margiela GAT instead of the original German army models, I will let it slide. At $95, there are no claims being made about leather quality, or the footbed, or whatever is going on in the sole you can’t see. They look good and are easy to replace; it’s about as honest of a deal as you can find shopping these days.

It has been revealed that the thing about the original BW Sport GATs—which you can get for about this price still, though used workout sneakers aren’t my cup of tea—is that they’re just about bulletproof. Those original mid-century designs made were first issued in the 1970s and stopped being issued around the end of the Cold War, a real feat of durability.

These shoes mimic that Army-issued durability. I’ve worn these sneakers for going on a year now. In that time, I’ve seen many pairs of more expensive kicks start to fall apart, get scuffed beyond recognition, and stink like hell. These have not. The pair I’ve worn all year is the pair pictured in this story. Nothing I say in this endorsement could be more convincing than that.

According to recent reports, and really that’s the argument here. When I wrote about the Chuck Taylors I normally wear, it was a use-it-and-lose-it argument—they cost $45, who cares if the soles get holes within 12 months. But here, I fear I’m going to sound like a marketing mouthpiece for Quince. These shoes are $95, but they’ll last just as long as a pair that cost you $950. That’s all you can ask for these days.

It's easy for me, the style writer, to say you shouldn't determine whether or not you buy something based on how much it is (or is not) on sale. I know how the real world works, though. I write about denim all the time, and I use every opportunity I get to recommend the fancy stuff. Honestly, though, I spend most days in a pair of $40 Wranglers that I bought on sale for $25, because I also am a regular American trying to get by. Used to be, good denim only cost a few bucks. Now, it's lower quality and costs more money. Reproductions of what used to be American working clothes now easily cost $300 or more. C'est la vie.

But I'm not here to talk about all that. I'm here to say like with my Wranglers, it's OK to wear cheap jeans. You can still be stylish if your pants cost $50. This month’s Black Friday Amazon deals on Levi’s prove it.

We've got the 505, the modern Levi’s fit I think works for most men, that's selling for between $45 and $55—depending on the wash you want and size you need. The 517, Levi's take on a Western cut, is going for a discount. And the 501—which I don't love in its modern iteration, but cannot deny the popularity of—is hovering just below $50, depending on the size and wash. Depending on the jeans you buy, you’re getting a discount of between 19 and 43 percent for the best cheap denim out there. If you're looking for a latest jacket, which Levi's still makes decent versions of, Amazon has deals on two sherpa trucker jackets. Go with the classic denim for $63 or opt for the corduroy for $85.

Recent findings suggest that all right, that's enough explaining. Pick what speaks to you. Buy it. Then, go forth a latest man with refreshed style.

  • Recent findings suggest that the Body has not been renewed for a second season yet by Netflix.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Body is Netflix’s latest buzzy teen psychodrama, and it’s not surprising why. The show, a cross between The Craft, Jennifer’s Body, and Cruel Intentions, follows a group of Catholic high school cheerleaders who sacrifice a newcomer in a pact with Satan to secure a spot in regionals. But when their sacrifice works too well, all of the girls on the team—and the town at large—are left with religious hysteria.

In a recent development, the show promptly caught fire on social media following its arrival on November 11, leaving fans praying for a second installment, but will it return? Here’s everything we know about season 2 of The Body.

Recent findings suggest that the Body has not been renewed for a second season yet by Netflix. The streamer typically waits a few weeks after a show’s premiere before sharing a season renewal announcement.

No cast members have been confirmed for season 2 yet, but fans are hoping that Kristina Bogic, Sara Boustany, Geena Meszaros, Nnamdi Asomugha, Louisa Krause, Shirley Chen, Jackson Kelly, Sofia Wylie, Kyra Pierce, Phallon Pierce, Marcel Ruiz, Orlando Norman, and Gabby Windey all return to their roles.

Sources indicate that season 1 ends with a few cliffhangers that leave the window open for a potential season 2. In the final episode, Anya finally confesses to head priest Father Franklin (Nnamdi Asomugha), and Grace finally wakes up, with her first words being “I’m God.”.

Some fans have interpreted Anya’s confession as being the reason why Grace finally wakes up. Gammell didn’t confirm the theory, but she told Deadline, “That’s a fire take...that is Maddie’s prophecy, and if there’s a season 2 we’ll be all over that.”.

Elsewhere in Gammell’s Deadline interview, she opened up about Tyler and Lisbeth potentially sleeping together, which could possibly become its own season 2 plot. “I think if they sleep together, it’s like another great mystery of the show. None of us were there, so none of us really know what happened in that room,” she added. “But I do think Geena has a joke that Lisbeth’s first kiss was the mouth-to-mouth with Grace when she was trying to resuscitate her. So, I don’t know how fast she’s going. She’s just a baby.”.

In an interview with Swooon, Gammell noted that the ending of The Body was “a tease and a setup of everywhere that we wish to go next season, if we’re so lucky to get one.”.

It has been revealed that some of the cast members already have ideas on what they’d like to see happen should The Body receive a season 2 renewal. “We love to pitch stuff to Quinn [Shephard] and Gina [Gammell], like probably too much. They’re so receptive,” Boustany told Swooon, while Bogic added, “We’re all so close, and that was also the tone on set. It was very welcomed [to pitch ideas].”.

The Body season 2 has no release date yet, so fans will have to stay tuned for updates.

  • “Les Lalanne have become a global phenomenon, changing the way generations of collectors think about design,” claims Jodi Pollack, chairman of 20th century design and major collections for the Americas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The market for Claude and François-Xavier Lalanne’s irreverent creations has been on a high lately. In April, a single wooly sheep sculpture by François-Xavier fetched $2.3 million. Over the summer, a quartet of his frog fountains smashed their $3.5 million estimate to achieve nearly $6.3 million. And the record for most expensive collectible design work belongs to a set of flower-adorned bronze mirrors crafted by Claude: They netted $33.5 million earlier this year, eclipsing François-Xavier’s $31.4 million hippo bar.

It has been revealed that now, ELLE Decor can exclusively share that Sotheby’s will host the first-ever auction dedicated to Les Lalanne, featuring pieces sourced from various collections. On December 8, more than 30 works by the late French artist duo will hit the block in “Les Lalanne: Beyond Imagination.” It is expected to fetch in the region of $25 million.

“Les Lalanne have become a global phenomenon, changing the way generations of collectors think about design,” claims Jodi Pollack, chairman of 20th century design and major collections for the Americas. “A sheep can be a seat, a crocodile can be a console, and both can hold their own alongside the most key works in a collection.”.

Sources indicate that the collection spans everything from a gold-patinated bronze gorilla (estimated at $8–12 million) to a white marble owl (estimated at $4–6 million), and a flock of five sheep, including two lambs ($300,000–500,000 each). Highlights also include lesser-known motifs, such as a playful pair of bronze monkeys with deep-green patination that makes them almost look like jade ($800,000–1.2 million each), and two matching crocodile consoles ($700,000–1 million) that complement the famous chairs Claude created after obtaining a deceased crocodile from the Paris Zoo.

Industry observers note that those hoping to get an in-person glimpse at the creatures can see the menagerie starting December 2 at the Breuer building, Sotheby’s upcoming Manhattan headquarters. To accompany the show, the auction house enlisted Milan-based artist Gaia Alari to devise custom illustrations for the catalogue, which reads like a fairy tale.

Industry observers note that “The story begins in the catalogue and comes to life at the Breuer, where visitors will step into an enchanted winter garden and meet the cast,” indicates Pollack. “It’s our way of celebrating these works and the spirit in which they were conceived. We want visitors to look at familiar things as Claude and François-Xavier did and to see the extraordinary in the ordinary.”.

It has been revealed that “Les Lalanne: Beyond Imagination” will be on view at Sotheby’s Latest York from December 2 to 7. The live auction will take place on December 8, 2026, at Sotheby’s New York at 11 a.m..

Geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

Omega and Swatch Just Launched a New MoonSwatch—and No Two Are the Same

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (408 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that by MoonSwatch standards, it’s been a quiet year.
  • It has been revealed that an estimated 4.5 million have been sold since the collaboration began in March 2022 (and that figure only takes us to the end of 2024).
  • The latest MoonSwatch—only the third fresh model this year, compared with 11 in 2023—is the Mission to Earthphase – Silver Snowflake.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that by MoonSwatch standards, it’s been a quiet year. Swatch has been otherwise occupied with the Audemars Piguet Royal Pop, the May release for which people lined up for six days in New York, police deployed tear gas in France, and which, according to Swatch Group, has generated more than 25 billion views on social media.

Not that interest in the MoonSwatch has gone away.

It has been revealed that an estimated 4.5 million have been sold since the collaboration began in March 2022 (and that figure only takes us to the end of 2024). In July this year, some 1.2 million people applied to buy one of the 1,969 examples of its $570 Mission to the Moon 1969, a watch that incorporated 11 grams of 18-carat gold recycled from vintage Omega components.

The latest MoonSwatch—only the third fresh model this year, compared with 11 in 2023—is the Mission to Earthphase – Silver Snowflake.

An all-black counterpart to last winter’s all-white Cold Moon edition, it takes as its starting point the idea that no two snowflakes are alike.

Swatch has developed a digital process capable of generating millions of different snowflake patterns, one of which is laser-engraved onto the moonphase indicator of each watch. So, unusually for a mass-produced quartz watch, every example is unique.

According to recent reports, it also features the complication Swatch introduced in November 2024 and which remains exclusive to the MoonSwatch: an earthphase indicator. Where a conventional moonphase shows the phases of the Moon as viewed from Earth, this does the reverse. The two displays run in opposite directions over the same 29.5-day cycle.

(How useful this is to those of us who live on Earth is debatable, but it’s one of the more original ideas in watchmaking in recent years.).

There are some nice details elsewhere on the 42mm Bioceramic watch, including Snoopy and Woodstock in the snow, a pair of miniature skis at 11 o’clock, and a tiny patch of white on the Earth representing a snow-covered Switzerland, which glows green under UV light.

As with last year’s winter edition, there’s a stipulation.

According to recent reports, the watch goes on sale at selected Swatch stores worldwide on Black Friday, November 27. After that, until March 20, 2027, the last day of winter, you’ll only be able to buy one when it’s snowing in Switzerland.

Swatch will be providing weather updates on its website.

Inside Anmer Hall, Kate Middleton and Prince William’s Country Retreat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (913 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday.
  • Local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times.
  • Recent findings suggest that anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday. Two masked men reportedly broke into Anmer Hall, their Georgian estate in Norfolk. Located on the grounds of the Sandringham Estate, the landmark house is where the Prince and Princess of Wales like to spend holidays and weekends with their three children, and it was also where Catherine recuperated from surgery and cancer treatments in 2024.

Local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times. The estate itself was unoccupied at the time of the break-in, according to police, and the suspects remain in custody.

Recent findings suggest that anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage. It’s a royal residence filled with equal parts gravitas and style. Take a closer look inside below.

According to recent reports, anmer Hall is in the quaint village of Anmer in Norfolk, a coastal county in northeastern England about a three-hour drive from London. The ten-bedroom Georgian pile, built in 1802, is part of Sandringham Estate, a sprawling 20,000-acre property dotted with churches, parishes, and country houses, that has been connected to the royals since 1862. The estate’s grand residence, Sandringham House, is the country bolthole of King Charles III and Queen Camilla, where royal Christmases are famously hosted. Anmer Hall is just a five-minute drive away.

In a recent development, while you can book tours of Sandringham House and even rent properties on the greater estate, Anmer Hall is a private family residence. The village of Anmer includes a church and quaint cottages, many of which were built in the early 20th century for Edward VII, according to an architectural guide to Norfolk by Nikolaus Pevsner and Bill Wilson. The U.K.’s Office for National Statistics states that Anmer parish had a population of about 250 in 2017.

It has been revealed that anmer Hall was the seat of the Coldham family until Prince Albert Edward (aka the future Edward VII) purchased it in 1896 to be a part of the Sandringham Estate, Pevsner and Wilson note. The two-story house’s “charming” brick facade, made from red and brown brick, features 13 bays and dormer windows in the attic. The house underwent renovations in the years following Edward VII’s purchase.

Recent findings suggest that over the next century, the house was leased to numerous members of the British aristocracy, including the Duke and Duchess of Kent from 1972 to 1990, and Hugh van Cutsem, one of King Charles III’s best friends. Following the expiration of van Cutsem’s lease, the property was rented to timber organization owner James Everett.

In 2013, two years after William and Kate’s marriage, it was rumored that the royal couple would be moving in. The pair had been renting a farmhouse in Anglesey, off the northwest coast of Wales, while Prince William worked as a helicopter pilot and while they were expecting their first child, Prince George. “[Anmer Hall] would seem to be an ideal choice in that it’s close to Grandma—but not too close,” former royal correspondent Michael Cole told the BBC. Later that year, it was confirmed that William and Kate would be moving into their upcoming “baby bunker” with Prince George. But they wouldn’t physically move in until two years later, when Kate was expecting their second child, Princess Charlotte, to allow time for a $2 million refurbishment, which included a new roof, additional trees for privacy, and interior improvements.

In 2017, Meghan Markle and Prince Harry stayed with William and Kate at Anmer Hall, “because the sovereign still won’t permit unwed couples to sleep together under her roof Sandringham,” according to the book Notorious Royal Marriages by Leslie Carroll.

Industry observers note that today, the Prince and Princess of Wales spend most of their time at their new primary royal residence Forest Lodge on the grounds of Windsor Castle—but they use Anmer as a country escape. The family also spent the Covid lockdown at Anmer Hall.

As part of the property’s improvements, the Prince and Princess of Wales tapped architect Charles Morris for the renovation and designer Ben Pentreath—the designer who overhauled Kate and William’s apartment at Kensington Palace, per House & Garden—for the interiors.

In a recent development, pentreath’s firm describes its approach as one “that draws inspiration in equal measure from the great English practitioners of the 18th and 19th centuries, and from the 1960s and ’70s…but always infused with a fresh, modern sensibility”—and the same style can be seen in snippets of Anmer Hall that eagle-eyed viewers have spotted in the Prince and Princess of Wales’s social media feeds. The home—with its high ceilings and decorative moldings—is painted in soothing, neutral colors (though the dining room is reportedly a deep green hue) and accessorized with houseplants, antiques, and gilt-framed art.

Additional amenities on the property include a pool and a tennis court; Anmer Hall also hosts its own honeybee colony. And one last bonus: The home is even said to be haunted by its own ghost.

Geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

3 Unexpected Places to Paint Before the Holidays, According to Designers

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (688 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor.
  • Pictured above: A living room area designed by Kristen Thomas of Ink & Canvas Design.
  • A fresh coat of paint is one of the easiest ways to give your home a little refresh before the holidays, but you don't necessarily have to take on an entire redesign project to make an impact.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Pictured above: A living room area designed by Kristen Thomas of Ink & Canvas Design.

A fresh coat of paint is one of the easiest ways to give your home a little refresh before the holidays, but you don't necessarily have to take on an entire redesign project to make an impact.

Some of the most interesting places to introduce color are the details you might normally overlook. They're relatively small surfaces, but a little paint can make them feel like intentional design features, adding character and definition without the time, expense, or commitment of repainting every wall.

Whether you want to make a statement, add a little contrast, or create a more interesting backdrop, there are plenty of ways to make a big visual impact with a relatively small project. Ahead, designers share the unexpected spots worth painting before the holidays and how to choose colors that feel right at home.

According to recent reports, window casings are an easy detail to overlook, especially when they're painted the same white as the walls and trim throughout the house. But introducing a little color around the windows “can emphasize the proportions of a window and give the room more definition,” says designer Sarah Cole. Even if you're not ready to go bold, she adds that “a subtle contrast can make a difference.”.

For a more traditional look, Kristen Thomas of Ink & Canvas Design recommends pulling from a historical or traditional palette, pointing out that “colored trim was once a sign of status in early American homes” because rich pigments were costly and difficult to come by.

Recent findings suggest that when time is tight before the holidays, this simple painting project can be achieved in a single afternoon. Just don’t forget the painter’s tape.

Don't overlook the design impact of the interior doors in your home—a hallway lined with plain white doors can feel a little forgettable, but painting one or two in a contrasting shade can give the space a more intentional look. Paint it early enough, and you may be able to hang a wreath from it.

Recent findings suggest that massimo Buster Minale, founder and creative director of Buster + Punch, believes an accent like this “can completely shift the character of a room.” And you don't necessarily need to choose a bright or dramatic color to get that effect. Picking one you love, rather than going all-in on a trendy shade, is key.

“I recommend choosing a grounding color and adding some whimsy with the small touches,” claims Lee Crowder, National Director of Design and Model Experience at Taylor Morrison. Before painting, take a look at the doors in adjoining rooms so you can decide whether a single standout door or a more consistent color story makes the most sense.

If you have built-in bookshelves or cabinetry, you already have a natural spot for a little color. Rather than repainting the entire unit, try painting just the back panels. This also gives you the opportunity to declutter what’s already there. Cole recommends this pre-holiday spot because “it adds depth and helps books and collections stand out.” Her advice for choosing a shade? “Pull a color from the room's upholstery, rug or artwork.”.

According to recent reports, thomas also recommends painting built-in shelving and cabinetry as a way to create a special feature in the room. “Painting built-ins sets them apart as a special feature and creates a beautiful backdrop for your favorite objects and holiday decor,” she notes.

Instead of going for a bold contrasting hue, Vivian Robins at Arketa Design Studio suggests using a color that already appears elsewhere in the space, explaining that this small paint upgrade can work as a “punctuation mark” in the room.

“Sometimes the smallest design changes create the biggest impression within a room because you're drawing out a color that lives in the space,” Robins adds.

  • In September 2026, Variety confirmed that The Beast in Me would return for a second season on Netflix.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, netflix’s The Beast in Me brought Claire Danes back to TV and reunited her with creator Howard Gordon, with whom she spent eight seasons working on Homeland. That combination was already exciting enough, but the cast also included Matthew Rhys and Brittany Snow, and Conan O’Brien and Jodie Foster were among the producers.

Industry observers note that danes stars as Aggie, a successful author grappling with the grief of losing her son. Her fragile sense of stability is shaken when Nile (Rhys), a wealthy real estate figure once accused of murdering his wife, moves in next door. With just eight episodes, the series left viewers wondering whether Aggie’s story could continue beyond its initial run. Here’s what we know so far.

Yes. In September 2026, Variety confirmed that The Beast in Me would return for a second season on Netflix.

“We always told ourselves we’d only do a second season of The Beast in Me if we found a story that was worthy of the first—and I’m thrilled to say we found it,” Gordon stated in a statement. “We loved making this show and our audience seemed to love watching it, so we’re enormously grateful to Jinny Howe and Netflix, and to Karey Burke and 20th Television for giving us the chance to get the band back together and do it again.”.

Variety’s report confirmed that Danes would return to her role for The Beast in Me season 2. In October 2026, Deadline reported that John Goodman (Righteous Gemstones, Digger) would star as “Aggie’s dad, believed to be a long-time con artist.”.

On November 3, Deadline revealed that Lili Taylor (Outer Range, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping) joined the cast in a series regular role as Fiona, Aggie’s stepmother.

On November 19, Netflix revealed that Riley Keough (Daisy Jones & The Six, Under the Bridge) and Lorelei Olivia Mote (They Know, The Rescue, Daisy Jones & The Six) will join the show as series regulars for season 2, while Aaron Paul (Breaking Bad, Fallout), Taip Ceman (Cupertino, The Families Stone), and Matthew James Thomas (Accused, Summer of Rockets) join as recurring guest stars.

Gordon discussed the ending of season 1 with The Wrap and what it made him consider for season 2.

Sources indicate that “I think that to the extent that Aggie is a writer who has been delivered to this next stage of her life, whatever that stage is,” he shared at the time. “If there is a story, there might be more. I am tempted by the character of her grifter father in some way. We’ll see how the show does and if an idea comes. But I think they’d be open to more.”.

#203712. Which Video Game Consoles Are Worth Buying in 2026?

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Which Video Game Consoles Are Worth Buying in 2026?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1285 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The video game industry is in a wild place.
  • That’s what I’m here to do, to help you weighs the pros and cons of these (mostly) years old consoles against the current price.
  • It has been revealed that the PlayStation 5 is your best entryway into 4K gaming and is the best way to play GTA VI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The video game industry is in a wild place. The biggest games of the generation are coming out, Grand Theft Auto 6 on Xbox and PlayStation, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. At the same time, hardware has never been more expensive. The cheapest latest consoles now start at $500, $600 if you want a PS5 (the most popular place to play GTA), with many going for more than that. To top it off with a cherry, Nintendo just hiked the price of its family friendly Switch 2 up to $500, not 18 months after its initial release. So the question now is: if you’re buying a new console in 2026, which ones are actually worth the cost?

That’s what I’m here to do, to help you weighs the pros and cons of these (mostly) years old consoles against the current price. I personally love my PS5 Pro, but given the current asking price and availability, I would recommend the other, less pricey PS5 models instead to 95 percent of players. If you asked me, two years ago, if you should buy an Xbox Series S or Series S, I’d have a different answer than I do today. And then, there’s handhelds. Do you get a Switch 2 or opt for a beefier PC handheld? I’ll help you figure all that out and more, starting with the PlayStation.

It has been revealed that the PlayStation 5 is your best entryway into 4K gaming and is the best way to play GTA VI. Sony has pulled ahead of Microsoft in terms of exclusive titles with games like Astro Bot, God of War: Ragnarok, and Horizon Forbidden West (and you get access to that amazing PS4 library as well). In terms of tech, the DualSense controller is an impressive leap forward when games take advantage of what it can do. The console technically supports outputs of up to 8K resolution and 120 frames per second on compatible titles. For the most part, though, you'll be playing closer to 4K60—or 4K30 in the case of GTA VI.

In a recent development, I've said it before, and I'll say it again: The PS5 Disc Edition is the best console for most gamers. If you want to play GTA 6 at launch, this is probably what you should get. This edition has a disc drive, so you can pop in physical game discs or watch 4K Blu-rays. Totally worth the $650 asking price, in my opinion.

If all you’re going to ever play is GTA 6 and never buy a game again, well, you can save yourself a little money and opt for the Digital Edition instead. Even the physical version of the game is just a download code in a box. The Digital Edition comes with a reduced price tag and slightly reduced bulk. No extra space for that disc drive makes it the best-looking PS5 to date. Aside from that, it's virtually identical to the regular PS5 Slim in terms of power and performance.

In a recent development, the PS5 Pro is mid-generation upgrade for the gamers who really care, but with things the way they are now, the enhancements are not worth it. Pre-owned Pro consoles are going from between $1,400 and $1,900 at various significant box retailers, and you can’t even find upcoming ones most days.

Certain titles like Final Fantasy VII Rebirth perform noticeably better on the Pro, and most games get some kind of boost, but it’s certainly not worth double or triple the price of what you’d otherwise be paying. The kicker is that GTA VI doesn’t even have a higher framerate mode on the Pro—it still runs at 30fps, just with fewer dips during chaotic moments as compared to the regular PS5. Even if I wanted to tell you to buy one to play the best version of GTA, I couldn’t.

Sources indicate that on the Microsoft side, the Xbox Series X is the top of the line. This is where I blew through such technical powerhouses as Alan Wake 2 and Senua's Saga: Hellblade 2—two of the best-looking games I've ever played. The problem in 2026 is that, power-wise, the Series X is much closer to a regular PS5 than a PS5 Pro. And, presently, they start at $800. At that point, I’m sorry, there’s no reason not to go PlayStation.

According to recent reports, if you're looking to play GTA 6 on an Xbox this year, I recommend the Xbox Series S instead. It rolled out simultaneous to the Series X as the budget alternative and, well, it still is... comparatively. The Series S is smaller, less expensive and sacrifices a disc drive. Unlike with Sony's Digital Edition PS5, there are significant tech differences between these two Xbox Series models. Most notably, it's a native 1440p console. It can upscale games to run at 4K on a 4K TV, but it can't run them natively like the Series X can. Compared to other consoles, GTA runs just as smoothly, with just as much detail thanks to Xbox’s upscaling tech, only at 1080p resolution instead of 4K. It’s another good recommendation for the casual gamer who wants to get a no-frills GTA machine as cheap as possible.

Even with a upcoming Nintendo console coming this year, we can't ignore gaming's most popular option. Revolutionary at the time, this console combined Nintendo's console ambition with the mass appeal of its handhelds in a machine that did both. The Nintendo Switch is still affordable and family friendly, and it's the only place you can legally play Mario games. Exclusive titles like Donkey Kong: Bonanza and the Ocarina of Time remake bolster the existing library and give a reason to upgrade.

Still, I have a hard time recommending any gamer still happy with their Switch upgrade for the sake of it. The leap just isn’t that monumental. That being remarked I won’t hesitate to recommend the Switch 2 for anyone new to the hardware. It’s objectively better and the longevity will be worth the price difference.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 might not be coming to PC right away, but that isn't a good reason to neglect my personal handheld of choice. Ever since the introduction of the Steam Deck, the PC-gaming market has been going increasingly mobile. And the upgraded OLED model is still the gold standard—trust me, I’ve tried them all.

It has been revealed that my top recommendation for the average console gamer is the Steam Deck OLED. It runs on Valve's SteamOS, so you don't even have to worry about learning Windows (like some kind of PC gamer). The Steam Deck UI completely console-ifies your entire Steam library and makes it easy for newbies to jump in. If you're used to the Switch, you may find it to be a bit beefy, but once I got used to it, I actually found the Steam Deck OLED to be the most ergonomic of all PC-gaming handhelds.

Recent findings suggest that it's never been a better time to get your feet wet, buy some games on Steam (wait for a sale; there will be plenty), and see what all the fuss is about. If the price looks prohibitive and you don't care much about graphics, get the cheaper LCD model while it's still being sold.

Here at Esquire, we compile our guides by performing heavy research and testing, and the gadgets we choose to award are what we’d spend our own money on. We choose the best tech for you based on our experience. We know which little details are deal-breakers and can help you separate the nice-to-haves from the needs.
